questions.question: Unlike other substances, alcohol:

options.text: Must be digested before entering the bloodstream.

questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested. It is absorbed directly through the stomach and small intestine and quickly reaches the brain.

questions.question: A motorcycle passenger should:

options.text: Put their feet on the ground when the motorcycle stops.
Not ride without a back rest.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver.
questions.explanation: A passenger should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the driver. Keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should not rely only on mirrors because:

options.text: Dirty mirrors can limit your view.

questions.explanation: You need to be aware of your surroundings beyond what mirrors show. Motorcycles have blind spots just like any other vehicle.

questions.question: You have a better chance of surviving a crash if you wear:
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards provides the best head and neck protection. Wearing a properly secured, quality helmet is the single most important thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, your arms should:

options.text: Have a large bend at the elbow when reaching for the handle grips.
Be slightly bent when holding the handle grips.
Be fully extended when reaching for the handle grips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be slightly bent when holding the handle grips.
questions.explanation: Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handle grips. This reduces arm fatigue and lets you press on the handlebars without stretching.

questions.question: To reduce serious injury in a crash, wear all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet protects against head and neck injuries. A leather or sturdy synthetic jacket also protects against injuries. A sweatshirt does not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: To shift to a higher gear, you must:

options.text: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift.
Place your foot over the shift lever and push.
Use your thumb to move the lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift.
questions.explanation: To shift to a higher gear, place your foot under the shift lever and lift.

questions.question: The front brake supplies about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a car's horn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's horn is not as loud as a car's horn. Use your horn when needed, but do not rely on it to keep you safe.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: May be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for the driver and passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. The motorcycle must have passenger footrests. Good footing helps prevent the passenger from falling and pulling you off as well.

questions.question: When can a motorcycle pass on the right?

options.text: When there is at least eight feet of clear pavement on the right.
By riding on the road shoulder.
By riding on the grass if it is level.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is at least eight feet of clear pavement on the right.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle may pass on the right only if there is clear pavement at least eight feet wide to the right of the vehicle being passed. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down, let the dog get closer, then speed up and ride away.
Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, let the dog get closer, then speed up and ride away.
questions.explanation: Dogs often chase motorcycles. If a dog is chasing you, slow down and approach it. Then accelerate quickly to leave it behind.

questions.question: How should a passenger hold on to the rider?

options.text: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
Do not lean into any turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to firmly hold your hips, waist, or belt. Your passenger may also hold secure handholds if they are available.

questions.question: In areas with potential dangers, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Cover the clutch and both brake levers to be ready to stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and both brake levers to be ready to stop quickly.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, schools, and construction zones, slow down. Cover the clutch and both brake levers so you can stop faster in an emergency.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They alert drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic is merging.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance when riding at night?
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distances in the dark. Keep at least three seconds of following distance when riding at night.

questions.question: How should the front brake be used?
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when slowing down or stopping.

questions.question: What helps other drivers see you on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing to make yourself more visible to other drivers. This works at all times of day.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift located on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your ability to ride safely?
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can hurt your ability to ride safely. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up ahead.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go.
You should drive through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you from behind, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side can be dangerous too — it may make the other driver return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders together.
Turn your shoulders, but not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go. Turn only your head, keep your shoulders still, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When entering a curve, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
Where you can see best and others can see you best.
In the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can see best and others can see you best.
questions.explanation: Position your motorcycle to see as far ahead as possible and to be seen by other drivers. For a left turn, ride on the right side of your lane to spot oncoming traffic early. For a right turn, ride left of center to see ahead without getting too close to oncoming traffic.
